To construct a number line, we choose a point corresponding to the number ‘0’. Points at equally spaced intervals are then associated with the integers. The positive integers are to the right of ‘0’ and negative integers are to the left of 0. All other real numbers are associated with a point which is called the coordinate of that point. The point associated with zero is called the origin. Usually few integers are shown on a number line to indicate the unit length of the line, that is, the distance between any two consecutive integers. Unit-01 Real Numbers National Book Foundation
